## Summary

Research confidence is **Low**. Sources do not yet confirm this break's best wind. It is the class the app computes from the evidence (how well the break's ideal conditions are documented), not a forecast and not a probability.

Main gaps:

- Sources disagree about the best wind direction.
- Sources disagree about the wave size this break works in.
- Limited information is available about the swell period this break needs.
- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the best swell direction.

Research notes (research_evidence.json):

> Wind is the main conflict, and the readable evidence now mostly contradicts the profile's northeast (45 deg). West to northwest is named as the ideal or best wind by Playground Surf Resort (W to NW), Yeeew (NW), Surf Indonesia (NW) and Botik Resort (NNW). Sumatran Surfariis explains that the wave sits at the SE tip of the island, so any north or east wind over about 5 knots ruins it, and it can be offshore in a west wind. Surf Camp Sumatra and Surfer Today (unread) say it needs, or starts firing with, some west in the wind. Indonesian Surf Guide and surftrips give E-SE instead. Only Surf-Forecast (NE) and WannaSurf (N, E, NE) support 45 deg. Playground's and Surf Camp Sumatra's texts share wording, so they are not independent. The profile's offshore wind should be reviewed; W to NW (about 270-315 deg) has the broadest support. Swell direction: S (Playground, Surf Camp Sumatra, Yeeew, Surf Indonesia, Botik), S-SW (WannaSurf, surftrips 180-225), SSW (Surf-Forecast), consistent with the profile; Indonesian Surf Guide's SW-W is the outlier. Size: 5-12 ft (WannaSurf, surftrips), 4-8 ft (Botik), head high to triple overhead+ (Indonesian Surf Guide) and chest high to triple overhead (Yeeew); the profile's 12 ft maximum matches WannaSurf and surftrips, while its 4 ft minimum is below the 5-6 ft most sources give. Tide: mid to high (WannaSurf, Indonesian Surf Guide, surftrips, Yeeew, Surf Indonesia, Botik) and high (Playground); the profile's mid_to_high is well supported. Period: no numbers found. Season: April-October (Surf Camp Sumatra, surftrips, Surf Indonesia), early season April/May (Playground), May-October (Surf-Forecast). Consistency conflict: Surf-Forecast ('very consistent') and WannaSurf ('Very consistent (150 day/year)') against Indonesian Surf Guide, Playground, Surf Camp Sumatra and Yeeew (3/10). surftrips says it was cross-checked against WannaSurf. No peer-reviewed, survey or official source found.

## Conflicting information

- **Swell height · minimum suitable**: Botik gives a size of 4 to 8 ft, WannaSurf says it starts working at 1.5-2 m / 5-6 ft and surftrips that below 5 ft it goes flat (none states face or offshore height), while the Indonesian Surf Guide and Surf Camp Sumatra say from head high and Yeeew from chest high (face heights relative to the surfer).
- **Swell height · ideal range**: Botik says it is best at 5 to 8 ft (scale not stated), while Yeeew says it gets good between chest high and triple overhead (face height), a much higher top end if the two scales are comparable.
- **Swell height · maximum suitable**: WannaSurf says it holds up to 4 m+ / 12 ft and surftrips gives a working size up to 12 ft, Botik's size range stops at 8 ft, and the Indonesian Surf Guide and Yeeew go to triple overhead (+) in face height; Surf Camp Sumatra says only that it can hold size.
- **Swell direction · ideal bearing**: Playground, Surf Camp Sumatra, Yeeew, Surf Indonesia and Botik say a distinct or best south swell (180 deg) and Surf-Forecast south-southwest, while the Indonesian Surf Guide says it works best with a SW to W swell (225-270 deg).
- **Swell direction · acceptable range**: surftrips says it switches on with swells from S to SW (180 to 225 degrees) and WannaSurf lists SouthWest and South as good, while the Indonesian Surf Guide's best range of SW to W reaches 45 deg further west.
- **Swell direction · exposure**: Surf-Forecast calls it an exposed reef break with very consistent surf, while the Indonesian Surf Guide, Playground, Surf Camp Sumatra and Yeeew say it is inconsistent or rarely breaks, and Sumatran Surfariis says large swells from the wrong direction make it too fast and it all has to line up.
- **Wind · offshore**: Surf-Forecast says offshore from the northeast and WannaSurf lists North, East and NorthEast; Playground, Yeeew, Surf Indonesia and Botik name W to NNW as ideal or best, Sumatran Surfariis says it can be offshore in a west wind, Surfer Today (search summary) that it fires when the wind goes west and Surf Camp Sumatra that it needs some west; the Indonesian Surf Guide and surftrips give E to SE.
- **Wind · onshore**: Sumatran Surfariis says the wave is open to any winds out of the north and east and is basically destroyed by more than 5 knots from there, which contradicts WannaSurf's good winds of North, East and NorthEast and Surf-Forecast's northeast offshore.
